newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICTSI, ICA win Ensenada port-SCT.
newsitem.headline: ICTSI, ICA win Ensenada port-SCT.

text.p: Philippine International Container Terminal Services Inc. and bidding partner Mexico's Empresas ICA were granted the 20-year operating rights to the multi-use terminal at Mexico's Ensenada port, a Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) spokeswoman said Thursday.
The source told Reuters an official announcement would be made later in the day.
After three rivals dropped out of bidding earlier this month, the consortium was the lone bidder for the port.

The winning economic bid, opened earlier in the day, pledged 25.12 million pesos for the service contract, 5.81 million pesos for the purchase of infrastructure and equipment and 2 million pesos for signing rights.
"Their proposal was much higher than the necessary minimum bid," the SCT source said.

Ensenada is a multi-use, commercial, fishing and tourist port in the northwest of the Baja California peninsula. It ranked second in the country in cruise tourist traffic and sixth in cargo traffic in 1993, the latest data provided by the SCT.
Infrastructure investments, such as a railroad to transport cargo to major consumption centers, are said to be needed to make the site more competitive with nearby San Diego port in California.
